# memory_note Usage Guide

<!-- socrates:section id="purpose" kind="purpose" tags="tools" -->
## Purpose

- `memory_note`: Send one short notepad lead to the Global Memory Agent only when the current turn contains an important durable memory candidate. Never call this tool for content the user genuinely instructed Socrates not to remember, save, store, retain, learn, or add to memory. Prefer one memory_note per user turn; the backend hard-caps distinct notes at two per turn and deduplicates normalized repeats. Input is only note and optional importance. Do not decide the memory target, skill scope, skill name, or action. The backend attaches the current user message and trace refs automatically.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="when_to_use" kind="routing" tags="tools" -->
## When To Use

- Use `memory_note` when the active task requires its cataloged read/retrieval capability.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="inputs" kind="schema" tags="tools" -->
## Inputs

- `memory_note` uses the one canonical schema owned by `tool.memory_note`; send only documented fields and do not add aliases or placeholder values.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="workflow" kind="workflow" tags="tools" -->
## Workflow

1. Select `memory_note` only for the behavior described above, pass an exact valid input, and use its persisted result as evidence before continuing.
<!-- /socrates:section -->
